alalal-c47451-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 17: how God is in all things without being defiled.

alalal-c47451-d1e113.summary: Asks why the soul is affected by the passions of its body but not defiled, sunbeams are neither affected nor defiled but touch spatially, and God is neither affected, defiled nor touching spatially, yet is in all things.

alalal-c47451-d1e133.summary: Reply: the soul's natural union with the body causes it to be affected, but since it shares no matter with the body it is not defiled. Sunbeams are neither united nor share matter, but are located, so they touch without being affected or defiled. God has no natural union, matter or position, so he is neither affected, defiled nor spatially touching, yet he reaches all by essence, presence and power, from end to end mightily in effect and disposing all sweetly in the participation of good, giving to each according to its capacity.
claims: God is in all without being affected or defiled because he is not united by nature, has no matter, and has no position.
God reaches all things by essence, presence and power, giving to each according to its capacity.

alalal-c47451.summary: Article 17 asks how God can be in all things without being defiled, comparing the soul, which is affected by the body but not defiled, and sunbeams, which touch spatially but are neither affected nor defiled. Albert explains that natural union causes affection, shared matter causes defilement, and position causes spatial contact. God has none of these, so he is neither affected nor defiled nor touches spatially. Yet he reaches all things by essence, presence and power, ordering them mightily and sweetly and giving to each according to its capacity.
claims: God is present in all things without being affected or defiled, because he lacks natural union, matter and position.
God reaches all things by essence, presence and power, giving each good according to its capacity.
